questions.prompt: A manager uses AI to summarize a project kickoff meeting and sends the output directly to the team without reviewing it. The summary lists the wrong person as the owner of a key action item. What is the root cause of this error?
choices: The AI model was not trained on enough meeting data
The manager skipped the verification step that is required because AI reliably confuses names and attribution
The meeting did not have a clear agenda, which confused the AI
The transcript was too long for the model to process accurately
questions.explanation: AI consistently struggles with accurately attributing who said what, especially when names or roles are similar. This is a known failure mode, not a one-time bug. Verification of names and owners is always required before sending an AI-generated summary.

questions.prompt: Which of the following meeting summary sections is most likely to contain information that AI invented rather than pulled from the actual meeting?
choices: Specific numbers, dates, or dollar amounts in the decisions section
The subject line of the summary email
questions.explanation: AI fabricates numbers most reliably. It will insert specific figures — dates, amounts, percentages — because they fit the sentence pattern, regardless of whether those numbers appeared in the transcript. Always verify every number in an AI-generated summary against the source.

questions.prompt: A manager wants to use AI to summarize a 1:1 conversation that touched on a team member's performance concerns and compensation. Which approach is correct?
choices: Paste the full transcript into the approved company AI tool only, never into a public model
Use any AI tool because the conversation was verbal and not officially documented
Ask the team member's permission before pasting the transcript into any AI tool
Summarize by describing general themes to AI without pasting any specifics
questions.explanation: Performance and compensation discussions are HR data. They must stay within tools your company has approved for that data category. Pasting such content into a public AI model — even one that does not retain training data — violates data handling standards and can create legal exposure.
